rows.name: HWATTN_MAX_B
rows.values: Integer number of queries, parsed with `atoi`. Only a value above `0` is used.
rows.default: Unset: the limit is the value computed for the FPGA card. It is at most 32 queries.
rows.effect: Lowers the largest number of queries (batch entries) in one hardware attention pass on an FPGA card. The result is the smaller of the value and the limit computed for the card. The variable cannot raise the limit.
rows.notes: `0`, a negative number, text that is not a number and an empty value count as unset. There is no error and no log line for the value. The value is read once per process. `rinzler_proxy` does not read it.

rows.name: HWATTN_WLR
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. A value above `0` forces the feature on. Every other value forces it off, also text that is not a number.
rows.default: Unset: each FPGA card decides from the project, version and release date of its bitfile. Empty: forces the feature off.
rows.effect: Forces weight-load reuse for hardware attention on or off for every FPGA card. The bitfile check is skipped. With reuse on, the driver tells the card to reuse its loaded weights when an attention command repeats the weight commands of the previous one.
rows.notes: The log shows `HW attention: HWATTN_WLR=<value> forces the feature ON by env flag` (or `OFF`). A forced `ON` is not checked against the bitfile. The log line `bitfile does not support HW attention WLR` ignores the variable. The FUSE stats file `/rinzler/stats/devices/<index>/wcmd_reuse/attn` counts reuse commands.

rows.name: PERFETTO_PRODUCER_SOCK_NAME
rows.read_by: `rinzler`, `runtron` through the Perfetto SDK (third-party code that is not in the repository). Also `perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh`.
rows.values: Path or name of a Unix socket. The Perfetto SDK parses the text. TRON code does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: the Perfetto SDK chooses the socket. `rinzler-capture.sh` expects `/run/perfetto/traced-producer.sock` when `/run/perfetto/` is accessible, otherwise `/tmp/perfetto-producer`.
rows.effect: Selects the socket through which the process sends trace events to `traced` (the Perfetto daemon). The socket is used only by a trace with the destination `traced`: the capture that the signal `SIGUSR1` starts, or `runtron` with `--trace traced` or `--trace-gen traced`.
rows.notes: `traced` must listen on the same socket. `rinzler-capture.sh` copies the value from the environment of the running `rinzler`. `TRACE_FILE` with a value other than `traced` makes the `SIGUSR1` capture write a file. The socket is then not used. TRON does not log the socket name.

evidence.quote: # The rinzler producer connects to whatever PERFETTO_PRODUCER_SOCK_NAME it was

rows.name: POS_1GB_PER_NUMA
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `atoi`: the number of hugepages for each NUMA node. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. There is no range check.
rows.default: Unset: `POS_NR_HUGEPAGES` applies when it is set. Otherwise the count is the `--nr_hugepages` value, or 16 hugepages. Empty: counts as `0` hugepages.
rows.effect: Sets the hugepage count of the process. With `--instance`, the count is value x NUMA nodes / 8, rounded down, then x S, where S is the number of physical slices (one FPGA card with its CPU cores each) of the instance. Without `--instance`, the count is the value.
rows.notes: Overrides `POS_NR_HUGEPAGES` and `--nr_hugepages`. The locked-memory limit (`ulimit -l`) caps the count. The divisor 8 is the constant `n_slices`. It stays 8 on a server with 4 physical slices. With `--instance`, the log shows `INIT: hugepages <count> (per numa <value>, per slice <S>)`.

rows.name: POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH
rows.values: Path of a file on a hugetlbfs mount (a file system that provides hugepages). The text is used as given.
rows.default: Unset: the `--hugepage_file` value, or `/dev/hugepages/libpos`. Empty: the path becomes empty. It is not treated as unset.
rows.effect: Sets the base path of the hugepage files. Without `--instance`, the process maps this one file. With `--instance`, only the directory of the path is used, and the files are named `slice-<k>-of-8`, one for each physical slice (one FPGA card with its CPU cores) of the instance.
rows.notes: Overrides `--hugepage_file`. Startup fails when the directory of the path cannot be read. When Dice starts the process (`DICE_DAEMON_CHILD` is `1`), the path must resolve to `/dev/hugepages/libpos`, or startup fails. The debug log shows `INIT: Allocating <count> hugepages from <path>*`.

rows.name: POS_NR_HUGEPAGES
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `atoi`: the number of hugepages for the whole process. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. There is no range check.
rows.default: Unset: the count is the `--nr_hugepages` value, or 16 hugepages. Empty: counts as `0` hugepages.
rows.effect: Sets the hugepage count of the process. The value is not divided by NUMA nodes or instances. With `--instance`, the count must divide evenly by the number of physical slices (one FPGA card with its CPU cores each) of the instance, or an assertion stops the process.
rows.notes: Ignored when `POS_1GB_PER_NUMA` is set, even to an empty value. Overrides `--nr_hugepages`. The locked-memory limit (`ulimit -l`) caps the count. A source comment calls this variable deprecated. The debug log shows `INIT: using POS_NR_HUGEPAGES. hugepages <count>`.

rows.name: POS_PREQUANT_CACHE
rows.read_by: `t_prequant_cache`, a test program (`h/tron/hardware/prequant_cache.hpp`). `rinzler` and `runtron` do not read it.
rows.values: Path to a directory. The text is used as given. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.default: Unset: the root is `<POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE>/prequant` when `POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE` is set and not empty. Otherwise the root is `/opt/positron/weights_cache/prequant`.
rows.effect: Sets the root directory of the prequant cache (a disk cache of quantized model weights). Only the test program `t_prequant_cache` uses this cache. The variable has no effect on `rinzler` or `runtron`.
rows.notes: Overrides `POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE`. The same header has a disable check that reads `TRON_NO_PREQUANT_CACHE`. Only the test calls that check. `bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py` writes this variable for the CI test jobs. A cache entry is stored at `<root>/<first 2 characters of the key>/<key>`.

rows.name: POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE
rows.read_by: `t_prequant_cache`, a test program (`h/tron/hardware/prequant_cache.hpp`). `rinzler` and `runtron` do not read it.
rows.values: Path to a directory. The code appends `prequant` to it. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.default: Unset: not used. The prequant cache root is then `/opt/positron/weights_cache/prequant`, unless `POS_PREQUANT_CACHE` is set.
rows.effect: Sets the root directory of the prequant cache (a disk cache of quantized model weights) to `<value>/prequant`. It applies only when `POS_PREQUANT_CACHE` is unset or empty. The variable has no effect on `rinzler` or `runtron`.
rows.notes: The variable plays no part in finding model weights. `POS_WEIGHTS_DIR` does that. `CHANGELOG.md` describes an older local weights cache under this variable. That cache was removed. `bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py` writes this variable for the CI test jobs.

rows.name: POS_WEIGHTS_DIR
rows.values: Path to a directory: the root of the model weights tree. The text is used as given. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: Sets the root directory under which the built-in weights name of a model, such as `<org>/<model>`, is looked up. It applies when a model is loaded with no explicit weights path. The path found is made canonical, and the programs read the model files from it.
rows.notes: `--model-path` does not use it. A relative `--model-path` is joined to the fixed root `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/`. A missing directory logs `Weights not found at the source path: <path>`, and the program stops. In `rinzler`, `GET /v1/info` returns the weights path of each model.

evidence.quote: TRON_ASSERT(!weights.path.empty(), "Couldn't find weights directory {} for model {}",

rows.name: REPO_ROOT_OVERRIDE
rows.values: Path to a directory. Any text that is not empty is used as given. The code does not check that the directory exists.
rows.default: Unset: the repository root is derived from the path of the running program. A program outside a `gen` or `gen-<variant>` build tree has no root.
rows.effect: Replaces the repository root that the program derives from its own path. The resource map (the YAML file that lists FPGA cards and CPU cores per server type) is then searched at `<value>/config/resource-map.yaml`. In a development build of `rinzler` or `runtron`, the default FUSE stats mount directory becomes `<value>/stats`.
rows.notes: Search order: `--resource-map`, `resource-map.yaml` in the working directory, this path, installed maps. With Dice, the map comes only from `/opt/positron/config/resource-map.yaml`. `RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH` and `--fuse-mount` override the FUSE path. A development build has `/gen/` in its path. The log shows `INIT: Successfully loaded resource map from <path>`.

rows.name: RZ_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS
rows.values: JSON object, at most 512 bytes. Each member value must be a scalar. `reasoning_effort` must be `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `xhigh`. `enable_thinking` must be a boolean.
rows.default: Unset: there are no server defaults. Empty: invalid. Every invalid value makes `rinzler` log an error and exit with code 1.
rows.effect: Sets default `chat_template_kwargs` (extra variables for the chat template) for every chat completion request. The defaults change the rendered prompt. `chat_template_kwargs` in a request override them key by key, and a top-level `reasoning_effort` in a request overrides that key.
rows.notes: Rejected keys: `messages`, `add_generation_prompt`, `bos_token`, `eos_token`, `tools`, `strftime_now`, `tokenize`, `continue_final_message`, `documents`. A valid value logs `Loaded RZ_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS: <JSON>`. `reasoning_effort` `none` or `xhigh` passes startup. Harmony models (gpt-oss prompt format) then answer HTTP 400 unless the request overrides it.

rows.name: RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS
rows.values: Exactly `1` enables. Exactly `0` disables. Any other text fails startup.
rows.default: Unset: enabled, the same as `1`. Empty: startup fails.
rows.effect: Enables or disables the request parameter `save_tokens` (it adds the rendered prompt and the token ids to the response). With `0`, a request with `save_tokens` set to `true` gets HTTP 400 with the text `'save_tokens' is disabled on this server`.
rows.notes: A bad value logs `RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS validation failed`, and `rinzler` exits with code 1. With `0`, the log shows `save_tokens capture disabled via RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS=0`. `RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1` together with `0` fails startup. The packaged unit `rinzler@.service` sets `1`. A value in `/opt/positron/user/config.env` overrides it.

evidence.quote: "'save_tokens' is disabled on this server", getPeerIp(req),

new_terms.definition: One FPGA card with the CPU cores that belong to it. The code divides a server into physical slices, and an instance owns one or more of them. The constant `n_slices` is 8.
The `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` limit of the process (`ulimit -l`). The driver converts it to GiB and does not map more hugepages than that.
The Linux file system that provides hugepages as files, for example `/dev/hugepages`.
A hardware attention feature. The driver tells the FPGA card to reuse the weights that it already loaded when an attention command repeats the weight commands of the previous attention command.
One entry of the batch that a hardware attention pass computes.
The third-party Perfetto library that rinzler and runtron link. The build downloads it. Its source is not in the repository.
The Perfetto daemon that receives trace events from programs over a socket. `traced` is also the text that selects this daemon as the trace destination.
A disk cache of model weights that are already quantized for the FPGA cards. The code is in `h/tron/hardware/prequant_cache.hpp`.
The YAML file `resource-map.yaml`. It lists the FPGA cards and CPU cores of each server type and how they are divided among instances.
A program whose own file path contains `/gen/`.
Extra variables that rinzler passes to the chat template when it renders the prompt of a chat completion request.
A request parameter of rinzler for development. The response then also carries the rendered prompt, its token ids and the output token ids.
The prompt format of the gpt-oss models. rinzler renders it with its own code path, not with a chat template file.

notes: POS_PREQUANT_CACHE and POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE: no product program reads them at this commit. The only reader is the test program t_prequant_cache, through a product header that only t/t_prequant_cache.cpp includes. The rows stay in this section with for=developers. They fit a test section better. TRON_NO_PREQUANT_CACHE is read by a check in the same header that only its own test calls, so it disables nothing at this commit. The row of that variable in another chunk needs the same statement. PERFETTO_PRODUCER_SOCK_NAME: the read is inside the Perfetto SDK v57.2. The build downloads that SDK, so its source is not in the checkout. No file under src/ or h/ contains the name, so read_by names no C++ file. The default socket paths come from the fallback code and the comment of perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh. The SDK handling of an empty or invalid value was not determined. POS_NR_HUGEPAGES: README.md lines 64 to 67 describe a second reader, the positron service, which is not in this repository. README.md says that service takes the value as hugepages per NUMA node. The TRON driver takes the value as the count for the whole process. The row does not mention the service, for lack of words. The document needs one sentence about it near the row. A comment in src/system/huge.cpp spells the name POS_NR_HUGEPAGE and calls it deprecated. POS_1GB_PER_NUMA: the divisor is the constant 8 also on a server with 4 physical slices (1 NUMA node). There an instance that owns all 4 slices gets half of the value. The row states the formula and this limit. POS_1GB_PER_NUMA and POS_NR_HUGEPAGES: no code checks for a count of 0 hugepages. The count then reaches the mapping call with a size of 0 bytes, and TRON_ASSERT(store != MAP_FAILED) follows that call. The rows do not state the result. It depends on the operating system, and nothing was run. POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH: an empty value gives an empty path. The cleanup step scans the parent directory of the path, and startup fails when that scan fails. The row states the general rule only. With a Dice grant, rinzler_proxy also checks the value (src/system/system.cpp), but it never uses the path. REPO_ROOT_OVERRIDE has two effects (resource map search, FUSE stats mount directory). The topic is weights. That topic covers where resource maps are found. rinzler_proxy gets the resource map effect only. RZ_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS: the JSON value null is also accepted and is ignored. Members with a null value are dropped. The rows leave both out. The term physical slice is the word slice of src/system. It differs from the glossary terms slot (Dice) and Slice (the test launcher).

changes.name: RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS
changes.was: A bad value logs `RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS validation failed`, and `rinzler` exits with code 1. With `0`, the log shows `save_tokens capture disabled via RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS=0`. `RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1` together with `0` fails startup. The packaged unit `rinzler@.service` sets `1`, then loads `/opt/positron/user/config.env`.
changes.now: A bad value logs `RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS validation failed`, and `rinzler` exits with code 1. With `0`, the log shows `save_tokens capture disabled via RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS=0`. `RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1` together with `0` fails startup. The packaged unit `rinzler@.service` sets `1`. A value in `/opt/positron/user/config.env` overrides it.
changes.why: The row said the unit 'sets 1, then loads' the file, which does not say which value is used. systemd applies EnvironmentFile after Environment (packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service:19-25, :43), and README.proxy.md:152-153 names the file as the place to set 0.
